page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-16-lssd is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c4n server family. This instance features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 16 dedicated vCPUs and a total memory capacity of 124.0 GB, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.75 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes local NVMe SSD storage, though the exact capacity is not defined in the storage size specification. There are zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this instance, and it does not feature any GPU accelerators.

From a resource density perspective, the c4n-highmem-16-lssd offers a high memory allocation relative to its compute cores, positioning it as a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring substantial memory footprints without the overhead of higher vCPU counts. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities. However, a notable tradeoff is the lack of benchmark data to verify real-world performance metrics, and the absence of GPU hardware limits its utility for acceleration-dependent tasks.

This server configuration is designed for memory-intensive applications. Suitable workloads include in-memory databases, caching layers, data buffering, enterprise applications with moderate compute requirements, and memory-heavy backend services.
